note: Piyadasi = Ashoka: NCERT XII Theme 2 (lehs102, pp. 28-29) and e-PG Pathshala ('Devanampiya and Piyadasi'); claims c02, c48. Practice q01 covers it.
Sandrocottus = Chandragupta Maurya: e-PG Pathshala §2.1, 'Greeco-Roman accounts mention kings Sandrocottus (Chandragupta)'; claim c38. Practice q37 (MATCH) covers it.

Megasthenes came to India in Chandragupta Maurya's time as Seleucus's ambassador: NCERT XII (lehs102, p. 32), NCERT VI (fess107, p. 65), e-PG §5.1; claims c07, c26, c42. Practice q11 covers it. Distractors Faxian and Xuanzang belong to HIS-08 and are not taught here, but the correct answer is fully taught.

Primary chapter HIS-00, but also taught here: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script of Ashoka's inscriptions (1837): NCERT XII Theme 2 §1 (lehs102, p. 28) and e-PG §2.2.1; claims c01, c54. Practice q02 covers it.

Primary chapter HIS-08 (Gupta period). 'Bisthi' (unpaid labour) is a Gupta-era revenue/labour term; it does not occur in any NCERT, IGNOU or e-PG source fetched for this chapter, so it is not taught in HIS-06.

Primary chapter HIS-08. The chronology needs Fa Xian, Xuanzang and Itsing, who belong to the Gupta/Harsha chapters (HIS-08). This chapter teaches only Megasthenes' position (Chandragupta's court, earliest of the four), which is not enough to answer the full ordering.

Megasthenes stated there was no slavery in India: IGNOU eGyanKosh Unit 5, §5.3 — the Arthashastra 'mentions the existence of the institution of slavery whose existence is denied by Megasthenes'; claim c69. Taught with the caution that the Arthashastra contradicts him. Practice q26 and q40 cover it.

Not fully taught: the chapter teaches that Ashoka's edicts mention contemporary foreign rulers (e-PG §2.2.1, claim c56) and that Syria's Seleucid king in Bindusara's time was Antiochus I (claim c45), but no NCERT, IGNOU or e-PG source fetched for this chapter names Antiochus II Theos as the Greek king of Syria in Ashoka's edict, so the specific identification the question demands is not taught and is recorded as a source gap.

'First historical emperor' is the exam's label for Chandragupta Maurya, taught here as founder of the empire (c. 321 BCE, NCERT XII, claim c05) who first politically united India under one king (e-PG §1, claim c65). Practice q03 covers the founder fact.
Primary chapter HIS-04 (Mahajanapadas / Alexander's invasion, 326 BCE). Alexander's invasion is not part of this chapter's scope and is not taught in HIS-06.
